description: Trigger evaluation set for the identify skill: requests that SHOULD activate profile interviewing, and near-miss negatives that should route elsewhere. Used by the develop trigger smoke test and by `develop optimize`.
should_trigger: help me populate my Working Style
my Personality facet is still all template, can we fix that
you don't really know much about me yet, let's change that
walk me through some questions so my profile isn't so empty
ask me questions so you can build a profile of how I like to work
should_not_trigger: what does the McAdams life-story method actually measure
update my Focus: heads-down on the launch this week
change my salutation to Dr. Lee
draft my bio for the company website
write up my working style as a one-pager for my team
what is the capital of Australia
summarize the article I just pasted
set a reminder for my dentist appointment tomorrow
notes: Positives are the named triggers plus the proactive case: a facet found thin or template-empty pulls identify in even when the user never says identify, in any repository or none (where the profile is kept is decided after triggering, by the repository's instructions). Near-misses are deliberately adjacent. A world-fact question about a framework (Big Five, McAdams) is research, not identify: identify asks the user about themselves, never about the world. A user-dictated update ('update my Focus', 'change my salutation') is a direct edit under the profile rules, no interview needed: identify is for eliciting, not transcribing. A prose file written under instruction ('draft my bio', 'write up my working style') is editorial's; identify keeps only the approved proposal batch. Generic clerical, arithmetic, and translation tasks are out of scope.
